meta.title: Hacking with Python: Your Guide to Ethical Hacking, Basic Security, Penetration Testing, and Python Hacking - Hacking Made Easy
meta.author: Evan Lane

sentences: **"Hacking Defined and Discussed"** – The introduction clarifies **hacking's** negative connotations, like **stealing info**, but also its positive role in **network defense**.
The book introduces key topics, such as differing **hacker types**: **black hat** (malicious), **white hat** (protective), and **grey hat** (curious/neutral).
Readers will learn foundational **hacking skills** using **Python**, emphasizing the importance of **ethical practices** over illegal system access.
This educational guide aims to demystify hacking, providing insight into **basic techniques** and ways to safeguard personal networks against intruders.
**Hackers** often target **passwords** as the weakest **security** link.
If not obtained through social engineering or physical **access**, hackers use tools like **Cain and Abel**, **John the Ripper**, and **RainbowCrack**.
These tools need physical access to the target system for efficiency.
Passwords are **protected** using one-way **hashes**, making them difficult for hackers to decipher.
**Linux systems** add complexity by using **salt** to randomize hashes.

parts.title: Evil Twin Attack Setup and Execution

sentences: **Setting up an Evil Twin Attack** involves creating a fake Wi-Fi access point that looks legitimate.
**Hackers use this** to trick users into connecting to it so they can **intercept and monitor traffic**.

The process involves using tools like **Airmon-ng, Airdump-ng**, and **Airbase-ng** to start up and conduct this attack, requiring patient waiting for targets to connect and then capturing their information.
**Deauthenticating targets** from their current networks and ensuring the strongest signal ensures that they **connect to the hacker’s fake network**.
